summary: Rung 2 of the PR ladder: committed .claude/settings.json permission allow-list (37 entries: read-only git/gh, collab.py context/audit/handoff, the project's own unittest/check.sh/run.sh/dotnet invocations -- nothing destructive per the task's explicit exclusions). docs/PITFALLS.md seeds 6 verified pitfalls (Godot first-run import segfault -- carried forward, not re-reproduced this session; CARD_INVENTORY.xlsx Excel lock; gitignored WebP working copies; the catalogue art pack's validate_coverage gate; PR #515's stale-base guard; .tools/.cache sizing, measured on this machine at 1.4GB/675MB). docs/ROUTED_CONCERNS.md indexes 6 existing engine invariants from docs/decisions/ and docs/rules/RULINGS.md as a separate file (AGENTS.md has a hard 12000-byte test budget with only ~1500 bytes of headroom, so a table there wasn't practical); linked one line each from AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.
validation: python -m unittest discover -s tools/content -p test*.py: 135 passed, unchanged. python -m unittest discover -s tools/collaboration -p test_*.py: 55 passed, unchanged (includes the AGENTS.md byte-size guard test). .claude/settings.json manually verified as valid JSON (37 allow entries). python tools/collab.py audit --working: clean. No .NET/engine tests run: no engine code changed (tooling/docs only).
remaining: None; ready for review, but the epic's literal Rung 2 done-when bar (a fresh session runs the standard loop with NO permission prompts) is only partially met by design, not by oversight: per this rung's own explicit constraint (no git commit, no git push, no branch/worktree creation, no gh pr/issue/label creation in the allow-list), a fresh session will still be prompted at git commit, git push/gh pr create, git switch -c/checkout -b (branch creation), git worktree add, and any gh issue/label creation -- every one of those is a mutating or visible action the task explicitly said not to allow-list. What IS now prompt-free: context refresh, PR/issue/CI inspection, collab.py context/audit/handoff, the project's test suites, check.sh/run.sh, and dotnet build/run. Closing the remaining gap would mean loosening those explicit safety constraints (not recommended) or a different mechanism entirely (e.g. a once-per-session confirm via a hook), which is arguably Rung 3's territory (hooks), not this rung's.
